extracted.intended_audience: national metrology institutes, government representatives, scientific instrument makers, and metrologists
extracted.subtask_description: Technical resolutions specifying how the International Metre and Kilogramme prototypes should be constructed, compared, preserved, and administered, and the institutional arrangements (Permanent Committee, International Bureau) to implement them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Starting-point for the International Metre
rubrics_metrics.description: As a starting-point for carrying into effect an international measure, the Commission takes the metre of the Archives, in its present condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The existing Archive metre is adopted as the baseline from which the international metre will be deduced and compared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deduction of marked/line metre from Archives standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission declares that, considering the actual condition of the platina measure of the Archives, it thinks the marked or line metre (mètre à traits) may be deduced from it with certainty. Nevertheless, this opinion of the Commission requires to be confirmed by the different processes of comparison which can be employed in this investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Committee accepts that a line-marked metre can be derived from the Archive prototype but insists on cross-checking through multiple comparison processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of International Metre's proportion
rubrics_metrics.description: The proportion (évation) of the International Metre will be deduced from the present length of the metre in the Archives, determined according to all the comparisons which have been made by means of the processes which the International Metric Commission will be in a condition to employ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All available comparison methods shall be used to determine the exact relation between the new International Metre and the Archive metre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and distribution of International Metre
rubrics_metrics.description: While deciding that the new International Metre ought to be a line-metre (mètre à traits), of which every country will receive an identical copy made at the same time as the universal prototype, the Commission will feel bound afterwards to construct a certain number of standards marked by projections (mètres à bouts) for those countries which desire them; and the proportions of such metres to the new prototype (à traits) will also be determined under the care of the International Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary international standard: a traced/line metre; optional projection (end-marked) metres may be produced and their relations to the prototype determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference temperature for International Metre
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Metre will have the length of the metre at zero (centigrade).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All prototypes are defined at 0 °C as the reference temperature for length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material composition of metre prototypes
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be employed for the manufacture of the metres an alloy composed of 90 parts of platina and 10 of iridium, with a margin (une tolérance) of 2 to the 100, more or less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify platinum‑iridium 90:10 alloy with the stated tolerance for manufacturing consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ingot casting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In manufacturing the measures, the ingot must be formed by a single casting by means of the processes used in the working of the known metals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prototype material should be produced from a single casting to assure homogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annealing of metres
rubrics_metrics.description: These measures will be annealed for many days, at the highest temperature — notwithstanding that they are never likely to be subjected to anything but the most feeble strains — before taking them to be compared with the standard instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prototypes must undergo prolonged high‑temperature annealing prior to final comparison to stabilize material properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimensions and cross-section of bars
rubrics_metrics.description: The bars of platina alloy upon which the line-metres are to be traced, will have a length of 102 centimetres, and their transverse section will be represented by the model described in a note of M. Tresca.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traced metre bars should be 102 cm long with Tresca‑specified transverse section (see Tresca note for shape).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of projection (end‑marked) metre bars
rubrics_metrics.description: The bars intended for the construction of the projection metre measures (mètres à bouts), will have a similar transverse section, but symmetrical in the vertical direction, conformably to the special figure which represents it; the knobs or projections (bouts) will then be wrought with a spherical surface of one metre radius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projection‑type standards require vertically symmetric cross-section and spherical end projections of 1 m radius per the specified figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support during operations and preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: During all the operations which the standard metres must undergo, they will be supported on the two rollers (rouleaux) indicated by General Baron de Wrede; but, for their preservation, they will be placed in a suitable case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specified two‑roller support for handling; store prototypes in protective cases for preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompanying thermometry for each prototype
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the International Metres ought to be accompanied by two mercurial thermometers, isolated, and carefully compared with an air-thermometer; it is deemed necessary that these thermometers should be verified from time to time by means of the air-thermometer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide two isolated mercury thermometers with each metre prototype, regularly cross‑checked against an air thermometer to monitor temperature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Fizeau method for dilatation
rubrics_metrics.description: The method of M. Fizeau will be employed to determine the dilatation of the platina alloy used in the construction of the metres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Fizeau's method to measure thermal expansion coefficients of the platinum‑iridium alloy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coefficients of absolute dilatation measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: The prototypes will be submitted to the processes by means of which the coefficients of the absolute dilatation of the complete metres can be best determined. These measures will be separately made, at five different temperatures at least, between zero and 40° centigrade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure absolute thermal expansion coefficients of completed prototypes at a minimum of five temperatures between 0 and 40 °C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter‑prototype comparisons at multiple temperatures
rubrics_metrics.description: The comparison of the prototypes with each other ought to be made at, at least, three temperatures comprised between these same limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare different prototypes with one another at least at three temperatures between 0 and 40 °C to establish consistent relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparatus for tracing and comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission decides that two apparatus be constructed, the one with a longitudinal movement for tracing these metres, the other with a transverse movement for their comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a longitudinal tracing apparatus and a transverse comparison apparatus to execute precise marking and inter‑comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison media and Archive metre handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The comparisons will be made by immersing new standards in a liquid and in air; but the standard of the Archives must not be immersed in any liquid before the end of the operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use immersion in liquid and air for comparison tests, but preserve the Archive prototype from immersion until operations are complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracing and first comparison by Fizeau process
rubrics_metrics.description: The tracing of the line or traced metres (mètres à traits), and their first comparison with the metre of the Archives, will be for the first effected by means of M. Fizeau’s process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial tracing and comparisons with the Archive metre should use Fizeau's method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of all approved comparison methods
rubrics_metrics.description: For the determination of the proportions of the various standards, there will be employed moreover all the means of comparison already known and approved, according to circumstances, either by actually bringing the different forms into contact, or by the method of Messrs. Airy and Struve, or by that of MM. Stamkart and Steinheil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ multiple validated comparison methods (contact, Airy & Struve, Stamkart & Steinheil, etc.) as appropriate to cross‑validate results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination by synthesis of observations
rubrics_metrics.description: The relations between the Archive metre and the new International traced metre, as well as the relations between the other traced standards and the International Metre, will be determined by comparing the results of all these observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synthesize results from all comparison methods to determine definitive relations among prototypes and the Archive metre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation of other standards from the International Metre
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations will be performed, on the other hand, by setting out from the International Metre for the construction of the standards with projections (mètres à bouts), which may be asked for by various states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the International Metre as the basis for producing projection‑type standards requested by countries, with proportions determined accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation of International Kilogramme from Archives kilogramme
rubrics_metrics.description: Considering that the simple relation established by the authors of the metric system between unity of weight and unity of volume is represented by the actual kilogramme in a manner sufficiently exact for the ordinary uses of industry, and even of science; considering also that the exact sciences have no real need of a simple numerical relation, but only of a determination as exact as possible of that relation; and considering the difficulties which would result from a change of the existing unity of metric weight, it is decided that the international kilogramme will be derived from the kilogramme of the Archives in its present condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain continuity with the existing Archives kilogramme rather than change the established unit; derive the international standard from the current Archive artifact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighing the kilogramme in vacuum
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Kilogramme ought to be decided by weighing in a vacuum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the mass prototype via vacuum weighing to avoid buoyancy and air‑related effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material for kilogramme prototypes
rubrics_metrics.description: The material of the International Kilogramme will be the same as that of the International Metre, viz.: an alloy of platina and iridium, as stated in No. 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the same platinum‑iridium 90:10 alloy for mass prototypes to ensure material stability and comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Casting and homogenization of kilogramme
rubrics_metrics.description: The material of the kilogramme will be founded and cast in a single cylinder, which will afterwards be subjected to furnace heat and mechanical operations, such as will give to its whole mass the necessary homogeneity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce the kilogramme from a single cast cylinder and perform thermal and mechanical treatments to achieve homogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kilogramme form specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The form of the International Kilogramme will be the same as that of the kilogramme of the Archives, viz., a cylinder whose depth is equal to its diameter, and whose corners may be easily rounded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain the familiar Archive cylinder geometry (height = diameter) with rounded edges for the new prototype.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of weight of cubic decimetre of water
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of the weight of the cubic decimetre or water ought to be made under the direction of the International Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission to oversee accurate determination of water's mass for definition/verification purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balances to be used and constructed
rubrics_metrics.description: The balances which will be used for weighing ought to be, not only those which may be placed for the present at the disposal of the Executive Committee by institutions and men of science who possess them, but also a new balance constructed according to conditions of the greatest exactness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use existing high‑precision balances where available, and build a new balance designed to the highest exactness for critical comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volume determination by hydrostatic method
rubrics_metrics.description: The volumes of all kilogrammes will be determined by the hydrostatic method; but the kilogramme of the Archives will neither be placed in water nor in a vacuum before the end of the operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hydrostatic techniques to measure volumes of kilogrammes, subject to the restriction of not immersing the Archive kilogramme until operations finish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of auxiliary kilogrammes for vacuum comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine the weight of the new kilogramme, in comparison with that of the Archives, in a vacuum, two auxiliary kilogrammes will be made use of, as nearly as possible of the same weight and the same volume as that of the Archives, according to the method indicated by M. Stas. Each of the new kilogrammes ought also to be compared in air with the kilogramme of the Archives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ two auxiliary artifacts matched in weight and volume for vacuum comparisons per Stas' method; also compare new kilogrammes with Archive kilogramme in air.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparing all kilogrammes to the International Kilogramme
rubrics_metrics.description: When the International Kilogramme is constructed, all others will be compared with it, in air and in vacuum, for the determination of their proportions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After establishing the international prototype, perform air and vacuum comparisons of national standards to determine their relations to the international kilogramme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison methods for mass standards
rubrics_metrics.description: For this purpose is employed the method of alteration and that of substitution, with a counterpoise of the same material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alteration and substitution methods with counterpoises of identical material to conduct precise mass comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections for weight losses in air
rubrics_metrics.description: The corrections for losses of weight in air will be effected by means of the most precise and least disputed data of science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply established, highly precise scientific data to correct for buoyancy and adsorption effects when comparing masses in air.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for making prototypes
rubrics_metrics.description: The making of the new prototypes of the metre and the kilogramme, the tracing of the metres, the comparison of the new prototypes with those of the Archives, as well as the construction of the auxiliary apparatus necessary to these operations, are entrusted to the care of the French section, with the concurrence of the Permanent Committee, provided in the following article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign operational responsibility (manufacture, tracing, comparisons, apparatus construction) to the French section under Permanent Committee oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent Committee organisation and powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission has chosen from its members a Permanent Committee, which will do duty till the next meeting of the Commission, with the following organisation and powers:—(a.) The Permanent Committee will be composed of twelve members, belonging to different countries. Five of these members constitute a quorum: it will choose a president and secretary, and will meet as often as it deems necessary, but at least once a year. (b.) The Committee will direct and superintend the execution of the decisions of the International Commission, in reference to the comparison of the new metric prototypes with each other, as well as the construction of balances and other auxiliary apparatus necessary for these comparisons. (c.) The Permanent Committee will perform the work indicated in (b) with all appropriate means which may be at its disposal; it will meet for the performance of its task at the International Bureau of Weights and Measures, the establishment of which will be recommended to the nations interested. (d.) When the new prototypes will be constructed and compared, the Permanent Committee will give a report of its work to the International Commission, which will sanction the prototypes before distributing them to the different countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a 12‑member international Permanent Committee (quorum 5) to oversee execution, apparatus construction, comparison procedures, operate via the proposed International Bureau, and report back to the Commission for sanctioning prototypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal to found International Bureau of Weights and Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission suggests to Governments interested how great would be the utility of founding at Paris an International Institution of Weights and Measures, upon the following bases:—1st. The establishment would be international and declared neutral. 2nd. Its seat will be at Paris. 3rd. It would be founded and supported at the common cost of all the countries which adhere to the treaty that might be made between the interested states for the creation of the establishment. 4th. The establishment will depend upon the International Metric Commission, and will be placed under the superintendence of the Permanent Committee, who will choose the director. 5th. The International Bureau would serve the following purposes:—(a.) It will be at the disposal of the Permanent Committee for the comparisons which will serve as a basis for the verification of the new prototypes with which the Committee is charged. (b.) The preservation of the international prototypes, in accordance with the directions laid down by the International Commission. (c.) The periodical comparison of the international prototypes with the national standards and with the tests, as well as that of the standard thermometers, according to the rules laid down by the Commission. (d.) The construction and verification of the standards which other countries may require in future. (e.) The comparison of the new metric prototypes with the other fundamental standards employed in the different countries and in science. (f) The comparison of standards and scales which may be sent for its verification, either by Governments or by scientific societies, or even by mechanicians and servants. (g.) The Bureau would execute all the works which the Commission or its Permanent Committee would require of it in the interest of metrology and the propagation of the metric system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend creation of an internationally neutral Bureau in Paris, funded and governed by treaty states, under Commission and Permanent Committee oversight, with explicit operational purposes (comparisons, preservation, periodic verification, construction/verification of standards, inter‑standard comparisons, and services to governments/societies/individuals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diplomatic approach to founding the Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau of the Commission is required to apply to the French Government, and request it to be good enough to communicate diplomatically the views of the Commission concerning the foundation of an International Bureau of Weights and Measures to the Governments of all the countries represented in the Commission, and to invite these Governments to conclude a treaty to create harmoniously, and as soon as possible, such an International Bureau upon the bases proposed by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permanent Committee/Bureau to seek French government assistance to diplomatically convene states and propose a treaty for creating the International Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple identical measures and invariant preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission is of opinion that the International Standard ought to be accompanied by four identical measures, maintained at a temperature as invariable as possible; another identical measure ought to be preserved, for the sake of experiment, at an invariable temperature in vacuo; it would take means to establish tests in quartz and beryl, to be compared at any time with the complete measure, in whole or by portions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain multiple identical copies of the standard under tightly controlled temperatures, keep an additional copy in vacuum for experiments, and use tests in quartz and beryl for comparative checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to re-measure a French geodetic base
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission thinks that in the interest of geodesy the French Government should cause to be re-measured, at a convenient time, one of the new French bases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform remeasurement of a French geodetic baseline to support geodetic ties to the new standards.
